High content of Tar and Nicotine in cigarettes sold in the country 
265. SHRI PRAKASH JAVADEKAR: Will the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY 
WELFARE be pleased to state: 

 217 
(a) whether it is a fact that various research suggests that 
cigarettes sold in India contain around 14- 15 mg. tar and around 1.6 to 
1.8 mg. nicotine; 
(b) if so, the reasons therefor when internationally observed 
permissible limit of tar is not more than 10 mg. and for nicotine is 1 
mg. in cigarettes; and 
(c) the proactive steps taken by the Ministry till date to ensure 
internationally advised and practiced level of tar and nicotine is 
maintained in Indian cigarettes? 
THE MINISTER OF HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE (SHRI GHULAM NABI AZAD): 
(a) to (c) Central Tobacco Research Institute (Indian Council of 
Agriculture Research), Rajahmundry has stated that in general the Tar and 
Nicotine levels in Indian filter cigarettes are in the range of 14 to 15 
and 1.6 to 1.8 mg/cigarette, respectively. It is also reported that a few 
brands with tar deliveries around 10 and less than 10 mg/cigarette and 
nicotine deliveries around 1 and less than 1 mg/cigarette are available 
in the market. 
Various countries have defined different limits of tar and nicotine 
under their respective legislation. 
The Government of India enacted as law namely "The Cigarettes and 
Other Tobacco Products (Prohibition of Advertisement and Regulation of 
Trade and Commerce, Production, Supply and Distribution) Act, (COTPA), 
2003, which mandate that every package of cigarettes or any other tobacco 
products produced, supplied or distributed may indicate the tar and 
nicotine contents on each cigarettes or other tobacco products along with 
the maximum permissible limits thereof. 
Neo-natal deaths in the country 
266. SHRI MAHENDRA MOHAN: Will the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY 
WELFARE be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government is aware that due to inefficient treatment, 
inadequate infrastructure and poor healthcare nearly 1.2 million newborn 
babies die in India within first few days after birth; 
(b) if so, the steps taken in this regard; 
(c) whether Government is also aware that neo- natal deaths are very 
high in north India, particularly Uttar Pradesh; and 

 218 
(d) if so, the details of schemes launched by the Centre in 
consultation with States to combat this problem? 
THE MINISTER OF HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE (SHRI GHULAM NABI AZAD): 
(a) and (b) As per Sample Registration System (2009) of Registrar General 
of India, Neonatal Mortality Rate (NMR) is 34 per thousand live births 
which translates to around 0.88 million newborn deaths in first month of 
life. 
Steps taken to address neonatal mortality rate are: 
1. Provision of facility based new born care through establishment of 
274 special newborn care units (SNCU) and 1124 New born stabilization 
units (NBSU) and 7413 new born care corner at delivery points. 
2. Training of medical officers, staff nurses and ANMs in essential new 
born care i.e NSSK (Navjat Shishu Suraksha Karaykram). 
3. Home based new born care: ASHAs are trained in 6th and 7th module to 
provide home based new born care. ASHA will undertake six home visits 
on days 3rd, 7th, 14th, 21st, 28th and 42nd (1 additional visit on 
1st day in case of home delivery) to visit the new born and for 
timely referral in case of noticing danger signs. 
4. New initiative named Janani Shishu Suraksha Karaykram (JSSK) was 
launched on June 1, 2011 under which sick neonate will be entitled to 
completely free treatment including free drugs and consumables, free 
diagnostics and free transport from home to facilities and drop back 
home. 
5. Infant and Young Child Feeding Practices. 
• Initiation of breastfeeding in first hour of birth 
• Exclusive breastfeeding till the age of six months 
(c) Yes. As per SRS 2009, NMR of India and Uttar Pradesh is 34 and 
45 respectively. 
(d) In addition to the schemes mentioned at (b) above, Uttar Pradesh 
has taken up Comprehensive Child Survival Programme (CCSP) in 36 
districts aimed at early recognition of danger signs and prompt referral 
for sick newborn.

at a price fixed by the Government or OMCs and have to prominently 
display stock- cum-price board at the place of business including the 
place of store at a conspicuous place. Under this Control Order, State 
Governments are empowered to take action against those indulging in 
black-marketing and other irregularities.Further, the Government has 
taken a number of initiative viz. Automation of Retail Outlets, Third 
Party Certification of Retail outlets, Monitoring of movement of tank 
trucks through Global Positioning System (GPS), etc. to check various 
irregularities/malpractices like adulteration, diversion etc. of 
petroleum products.

Retail Outlets and also take action under Marketing Discipline Guidelines

seals, and unauthorized fittings/gears in dispensing units.

Production cost of gas from KG Basin 
287. SHRI P. RAJEEVE: Will the Minister of PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS 
be pleased to state: 
(a) the production cost of retrieving natural gas from the KG Basin; 
(b) the difference between international and domestic costs; and 
(c) the price at which Reliance Industries Ltd. (RIL) is allowed to 
extract gas from the KG Basin? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS 
(SHRI R.P.N. SINGH): (a) and (b) In India, natural gas is produced by 
National Oil Companies/State PSUs, Private & Foreign companies. 
Production cost of natural gas by the Operators is dependent on various 
factors such as geological prospectively, reservoir parameters & 
performance, terrain such as on- land / shallow water / deep water / 
ultra-deep water, development concept, well productivity, calorific value 
of the natural gas, input costs, work efficiency of the individual 
companies etc. It also varies over a period of time. Hence, it is not 
feasible to arrive at a definite natural gas production cost for any 
field/basin. For the same reason, comparison cannot be done with 
international prices. 
(c) The Empowered Group of Ministers (EGoM), after considering the 
price proposal submitted by the parties, has approved a price formula for 
the gas produced in the block KG- DWN-98/3 contracted to RIL- NIKO 
Consortium, in its meeting held on 12.9.2007 for 5 years from the date of 
commencement of supply. The details of the formula is as under: 
SP (USD/mmbtu) - 2.5+(CP-25)^0.15 
Where SP = Selling Price 
CP = Crude Price 
The cap for CP in the formula has been frozen at US $ 60 per barrel. 
The price obtained from the basis/formula comes to US $ 4.2 per Million 
Metric British Thermal Unit (MMBTU) for crude oil price equal or greater 
than US $ 60 per barrel.

Advisory to Gram Panchayats 
296. SHRI A. ELAVARASAN: Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be 
pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government has issued an advisory to Gram Panchayats 
making it mandatory for them to convene Gram Sabhas regularly; 
(b) if so whether the initiative is aimed at making the projects run 
under MGNREGA less centralized; 
(c) whether there is a provision in the Act which requires 
Panchayats convene such meetings and make proactive disclosures but many 
Panchayats are not implementing it; 
(d) if so, the details there of; 
(e) whether several faults in its implementation and lack of 
mandatory proactive disclosures by the local bodies have been found 
during the performance audit by CAG and Government is trying to rectify 
it now; and 
(f) if so, the detail thereof? 

 269 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT (SHRI 
PRADEEP JAIN): (a) to (d) Gram Panchayats have been given pivotal role in 
registration and issue of job cards, accepting applications for work and 
issue of dated receipts, providing work to the applicant, maintenance of 
records, identification of projects as per recommendations of Gram 
Sabha/Ward Sabha, preparation of development plan and maintain shelf of 
projects under various provisions of MGNREG Act. In accordance with 
Section 16(5) of the Act, at least 50% of the projects by cost are to be 
executed by the Gram Panchayats. Section 13(1) of Mahatma Gandhi NREGA 
provides that the Panchayats at district, intermediate and village levels 
shall be the principal authorities for planning and implementation of the 
schemes made under the Act. 
Section 16(1) of Mahatma Gandhi NREGA provides that Gram Panchayats 
shall be responsible for identification of projects in the Gram Panchayat 
area to be taken up under the scheme as per the recommendations of the 
Gram Sabha and Ward Sabhas. Section 17(2) of Mahatma Gandhi NREGA 
provides that Gram Sabha shall conduct regular social audits of all the 
projects under the Scheme taken up within the Gram Panchayat. Social 
Audit is an on going process and is to be held at least once in every six 
months. The Ministry has accorded utmost importance to the organization 
of Social Audits by the Gram Panchayats and issued instructions to the 
States to make necessary arrangements for the purpose. The Ministry has 
also issued advisory to the States to open adequate works to ensure full 
enjoyment of rights by the rural households under Mahatma Gandhi NREGA. 
(e) and (f) In order to rectify faults and shortcoming in 
implementation and proactive disclosures by local bodies observed during 
performance audits, the Ministry has, in consultation with the 
Comptroller & Auditor General of India, notified on 30th June, 2011, the 
Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Audit of Schemes 
Rules, 2011, which includes Social Audit by Gram Sabhas: 
The salient features of the said rules are: 
• Every Gram Panchayat to have at least one social audit every six 
months; 
• Social Audit Units to facilitate verification of records with primary 
stakeholders and work sites; 
• Gram Sabha shall be convened to discuss the findings of the 
verification exercise and also to review the compliance on 

 270 
transparency and accountability, fulfilment of the rights and 
entitlements of labourers and proper utilisation of funds; 

 271 
• The Gram Sabha shall provide a platform to all villagers to seek and 
obtain further information and responses from all involved in the 
implementation; 
• Summary of findings of social audit to be submitted by the State 
Government to the Comptroller & Auditor General of India.

CBI investigation in MGNREGS fund scam 
300. PROF. ANIL KUMAR SAHANI: Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
be pleased to state: 
(a) whether there has been corruption in the utilization of Mahatma 
Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme (MGNREGS) funds in 
Orissa and CBI is investigating the said scam; 
(b) whether CBI has submitted its report; 
(c) if so, the details thereof and the actions taken thereon; 
(d) whether Government has conducted any study in States to 
ascertain that the MGNREGS funds are being used for the stipulated 
purposes only; 
(e) if so, the findings of that study; and 
(f) the details of complaints received by Government from MPs and 
common man concerning corruption in MGNREGS together with action taken 
thereon? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT (SHRI 
PRADEEP JAIN): (a) to (c) A total of 58 complaints regarding 
irregularities, including corruption, in the implementation of Mahatma 
Gandhi NREGA in Orissa have been received in the Ministry. Out of these, 
26 cases have been disposed off so far. The complaints mainly relate to 
cases of job cards not provided, misappropriation of funds, engagement of 
contractors, forgery of muster roll, manipulation in job cards, under 
payment of wages, non- payment of wages, corruption and other 
irregularities, use of machinery, delay in payments etc. On receipt of 
consent of the State Government of Orissa in April 2011, the Union 
Government ordered an investigation by the Central Bureau of 
Investigation (CBI) into allegations of corruption and misappropriation 
of funds under MGNREGA in Orissa. CBI has not submitted its report in the 
matter. 
(d) and (e) No separate study has been conducted to ascertain that 
MGNREGS funds are being used for the stipulated purposes. However, there 
are mechanisms of internal and social audits, visits by National Level 
Monitors and Eminent Citizens, etc in the scheme to ensure that funds are 
utilized for the purposes envisaged in MGNREG Act. 

 274 
(f) A total of 2250 complaints regarding irregularities, including 
corruption, in the implementation of Mahatma Gandhi NREGA in the country 
have been received in the Ministry as on 26.7.2011. Out of these, 1003 
cases have been disposed off. As implementation of the Act is done by the 
State Governments in accordance with the Schemes formulated by them as 
per the provisions of the Act, all complaints received in the Ministry 
are forwarded to the concerned State Governments for taking appropriate 
action as per law. In complaints of serious nature, the Ministry deputes 
National Level Monitors (NLMs) to investigate the complaints. Reports of 
the NLMs are shared with the concerned State Governments for taking 
corrective action.

†303. SHRI RUDRA NARAYAN PANY: Will the Minister of RURAL 
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that recently arable land is being acquired 
on a large scale throughout the country for the purpose of industrial 
development; 
(b) whether it is also a fact that grave discontentment has spread 
among the people therefor; 
(c) if so, the details thereof; and

so far to address this discontentment, agitation, lathi charge, firing, 
violence and tumult etc. regarding land acquisition throughout the 
country?

SISIR ADHIKARI): (a) to (d) Land and its management are under the 
exclusive legislative and administrative jurisdiction of the States as 
provided in Entry No. 18 of List II ( State list ) of the Seventh 
Schedule to the Constitution. Acquisition of arable/agricultural land for 
various Industrial development projects is being done by the concerned 
State Governments. The Land Acquisition Act, 1894 lays down certain 
criteria for acquisition of land for public purposes and for companies. 
Land

acquisition is being done by the States as per the provisions of this 
law. There have been agitation against the Land Acquisitions which are 
being handled by the State Governments. Amendment of Land Acquisition 
Act, 1894 is under consideration of the Government. This department is 
finalizing an integrated Land Acquisition and Rehabilitation & 
Resettlement Bill, 2011 to address various issues related to land 
acquisition and rehabilitation & resettlement.

Memorandum on irregularities in MGNREGS works in Bilaspur 
305. SHRIMATI BRINDA KARAT: Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be 
pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government has received any memorandum from Bilaspur 
District, Chhattisgarh regarding irregularities and corruption, involving 
an amount over 200 crores, in Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment 
Guarantee Scheme (MGNREGS) works; and 

 287 
(b) if so, the steps taken by Government so that those guilty of 
embezzlement of the public money meant for the poor could be severely 
punished? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT (SHRI 
PRADEEP JAIN): (a) Yes Sir. 
(b) A memorandum dated 3/12/2010 alleging corruption involving over 
Rs.200 crore in implementation of Mahatma Gandhi National Rural 
Employment Guarantee Scheme (MGNREGS) works in Vilaspur District of 
Chhattisgarh received in the Ministry was referred to the State 
Government on 31/12/2010 for examination and action taken report. No 
response was received from the State Government even after reminder from 
the Ministry dated 11/3/2011. This complaint/matter was examined in the 
Ministry in May, 2011 and a team of two National Level Monitors (NLMs) 
was deputed to investigate the complaint and submit a report. The report 
of NLMs has been received in the last week of July, 2011. The report is 
being sent to the State Government for taking action. As implementation 
of the MGNREG Act is done by the States Government in accordance with the 
Schemes formulated by them as per the provisions of the Act, all 
complaints received in the Ministry are forwarded to the concerned States 
for taking appropriate action as per law. In complaints of serious 
nature, the Ministry deputes National Level Monitors to investigate the 
complaints. Reports of the NLMs are shared with the concerned State 
Governments for taking corrective action. 
Improving the performance of MGNREGS in backward States 
306. SHRI PARIMAL NATHWANI: Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be 
pleased to state: 
(a) whether the performance of Mahatma Gandhi National Rural 
Employment Guarantee Scheme (MGNREGS) has remained tardy in States where 
poverty rate is high; 
(b) if so, the details of such States and the reasons for tardy 
performance of the scheme there; and 
(c) the steps taken by Government to make MGNREGS more effective in 
backward States? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT (SHRI 
PRADEEP JAIN): (a) to (c) Mahatma Gandhi NREGA is demand driven. 
Employment is provided to a  

 288 
registered household having a job card on demand. MGNREGA provides for a 
legal guarantee for up to 100 days of wage employment to every rural 
household in every financial year for doing unskilled manual work on 
demand. The Act provides that work has to be provided to an applicant 
within 15 days of the demand. In 2010- 11. 5.49 crore households were 
provided employment under MGNREGA. The efforts made by the Government to 
make MGNREGS more effective and improve performance in States under the 
scheme include the following measures: 
(i) Permissible administrative expenditure limit has been enhanced from 
4% to 6% for deployment of dedicated staff for MGNREGA, strengthening 
of management and administrative support structures for social audit, 
grievance redressal and ICT infrastructure. 
(ii) Instructions have been issued on 7.9.09 directing all States to 
appoint ombudsman at district level for grievance redressal. 
(iii) Social audit: The Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment 
Guarantee Audit of Schemes Rules, 2011 have been notified in the 
Gazette on 30th June, 2011. 
(iv) ICT based MIS has been made operational to make data available to 
public scrutiny including Job cards, Muster rolls, Employment 
demanded and allocated, number of days worked, shelf of works, Funds 
available/spent and funds released to various implementing agencies, 
Social Audit findings, registering grievances and generating alerts 
for corrective action. 
(v) Payment of wages to MGNREGA workers has been made mandatory through 
their accounts in Banks/Post Office to infuse transparency in wage 
disbursement. 
(vi) District Excellence Award for districts with outstanding performance 
under MGNREGA. 
(vii) Rozgar Jagrookta Puraskar for NGOs working towards effective 
implementation of MGNREGA.
